plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, truthful bidding (bidding exactly my value) is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than my value (negative profit), and if I bid lower, I risk losing an auction I could have profitably won. Since I pay the second-highest bid rather than my own bid, there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Therefore, my optimal action is simply to bid my true value of $48.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks winning at a loss, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $38, I should bid exactly $38 to maximize expected profit, as this strategy is optimal regardless of the other bidders' rationality or beliefs about me.
